# Hermes Agent: Comprehensive FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

### 1. Installation, Environment & Platform Support

**Q: What platforms are supported?**
- **Native Windows**: Tier 1 supported via `install.ps1`. (WSL2 is recommended only if using the Web Dashboard `/chat` embedded terminal, which requires a POSIX PTY).
- **Docker / NAS**: Official multi-arch image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` supports `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Raspberry Pi, Apple Silicon). For NAS permission errors (`[Errno 13] Permission denied` on UGOS, Synology, unRAID), pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) to remap container user permissions.
- **Android (Termux)**: Detected automatically by `install.sh`. Uses writable `$TMPDIR` and installs curated `[termux-all]` dependencies.
- **Web Interface**: Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local UI at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`.

**Q: Why does `hermes update` hang on the Node.js dependency step?**
This occurs during the Camofox post-install step, which downloads a browser binary in the background without progress output.

---

### 2. Model Providers, Configuration & Billing

**Q: Why are small local models (Qwen 4B–9B / Ollama) responding very slowly?**
Hermes sends the full tool schema (~45 tools) on every turn, overwhelming small context-processing capacities. Optimize by:
- Disabling unneeded tools via `hermes tools`.
- Setting `terminal.backend: local` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to remove container overhead.
- Using faster quantizations or larger models (32B+).

**Q: Why does Hermes ignore my local endpoint (`localhost:11434`) and throw 401 errors?**
When `provider: auto` is set, Hermes prioritizes discovered environment variables (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Explicitly configure `provider: custom`:
```yaml
model:
  default: ollama/your-model
  provider: custom
  base_url: http://localhost:11434
fallback_providers: []
```

**Q: How do I configure specific model providers?**
- **Claude Pro/Max vs API**: API keys are billed per token by Anthropic. To consume Pro/Max subscription quota instead, authenticate via Claude OAuth.
- **Google Gemini**: Legacy CLI OAuth and `google-antigravity` were removed due to upstream restrictions. Use Google AI Studio (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`) or Vertex AI.
- **Ollama Cloud**: Set provider to `ollama-cloud` (routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`).
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Run `hermes setup` or set `provider: azure-foundry` with `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`.
- **LocalAI / OpenAI-compatible Token Tracking**: Hermes automatically passes `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` on streaming endpoints.
- **Custom Vision Models**: Add `supports_vision: true` under your custom model config.
- **Model Cost Normalization**: DeepSeek V4 canonical names (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) pass through without unwanted rewriting.

**Q: Does Hermes support automatic cheap/strong model routing?**
No. Complexity-based automatic model routing (`smart_model_routing`) is intentionally rejected by maintainer policy. Use manual switching (`/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`) or subagent delegation (`delegation.provider` / `delegation.model`).

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways & Personas

**Q: How do I set up and authorize messaging platforms?**
Run `hermes gateway setup` for an interactive wizard (Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc.).
- **Telegram Authorization**: `allowed_chats` is only a group whitelist; `guest_mode: true` only allows group @mentions. To authorize direct messages, add your numeric user ID to `allow_from` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, approve pairing via `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `allow_all: true`.
- **Discord**: Interactive setup safely prompts for `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`.

**Q: Can gateways send and receive files, images, and tool progress?**
- **Inbound Files**: Uploaded text/code files (`.py`, `.txt`) are automatically injected into context; other files are cached.
- **Outbound Media**: Supports email attachments, Matrix `m.file` uploads, DingTalk Markdown images (`![image](url)`), and Telegram media. MCP base64 images tagged with `MEDIA:<path>` are forwarded natively.
- **Open WebUI**: Tool execution progress is streamed via SSE (`v2026.4.8+`).

**Q: How do multi-agent delegation and per-channel personas work?**
- **Subagents**: Use `delegate_task` to spawn isolated child `AIAgent` instances (default up to 3 concurrent).
- **Per-Channel Persona**: Configure `channel_prompts` with channel IDs in platform settings (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost).
- **Multi-Profile Multiplexing**: Run multiple profile gateways simultaneously with isolated sessions, memory, and credentials.

---

### 4. Memory, Tools & Context Management

**Q: How are memory files structured and configured?**
- `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Agent identity, backstory, and system persona.
- `~/.hermes/USER.md`: User profile, identity, and personal preferences (`target="user"`).
- `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md`: Long-term persistent world knowledge.
- **Local Honcho**: Points to local URLs (`http://localhost:8000`) without an API key by auto-injecting a `"local"` placeholder (`v2026.3.30+`).
- **Memory Plugins**: In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. External memory plugins must implement the `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`, optional `post_setup`) in `~/.hermes/plugins/`.

**Q: How do I add custom tools?**
Personal tools should be created in `~/.hermes/plugins/` via `ctx.register_tool(...)` and enabled using `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Core built-in tools reside in `tools/*.py` and must be exposed in `toolsets.py`.

**Q: How does context compression and autonomous execution work?**
- **Context Management**: `ContextCompressor` automatically prunes and deduplicates historical tool outputs. Custom engines can be configured via `context.engine`.
- **Tool Limits**: Controlled by `agent.max_turns` (default 90; CLI override `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). Once hit, the agent finalizes its response without tools.
- **Persistent Autonomy**: Use `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop) for long tasks across turns; resume paused tasks with `/goal resume`.
- **Session Restores**: Interrupted sessions are flagged as `resume_pending`. Run `/resume` to restore conversation history. Default session reset mode is `none`.

---

### 5. Telemetry, Observability & Security

- **System Health**: Run `hermes doctor` to verify environment, dependencies, and credentials.
- **Skill Tracking**: Load and usage metrics are saved in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json` and viewed via `/insights` or `hermes insights`.
- **Tracing**: Enable Langfuse observability with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Security Disclosures**: Report security vulnerabilities privately via GitHub Security Advisories or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com`.
